articles.title: Viking 1’s First Mars Photo Turns 50: The Pixelated Image That Changed Planetary Science Forever
articles.summary: Fifty years ago, a spacecraft called Viking 1 transmitted the first image from the surface of another planet. The grainy, black-and-white photo revealed a rocky Martian landscape — and a piece of the lander itself, proving humanity had touched another world. But the mission’s biggest question — did it find life? — remains unanswered.

articles.title: Sony’s Disc Era Is Ending — Here’s Your Last Chance to Snag Physical PS5 Games at a Steal
articles.summary: With Sony confirming that the PS5 will be its last console with a disc drive, physical game collectors are facing a deadline. But a massive sale across major retailers is offering steep discounts on first-party PS5 exclusives — including Spider-Man 2 for $30 and Death Stranding 2 for $40 — making now the ideal time to stock up.

articles.title: Why Earth Is the Ultimate Cosmic Oasis — and Still Full of Surprises
articles.summary: Earth isn’t just our home — it’s a planetary jackpot. With liquid water, a life-shielding atmosphere, and a magnetic field that sparks auroras, it’s uniquely suited for life. Yet we’ve mapped more of Mars than our own ocean floors, proving this world still holds deep mysteries.
